sentences.text: The type species Dianchungosaurus lufengensis was described in 1982 after fossils were found in the Lower Lufeng Formation near Dianchung in Yunnan Province, China.
These remains date to the Sinemurian stage of the Early Jurassic, placing the animal between 199.5 and 192.9 million years ago.
Dianchungosaurus was originally thought to be a dinosaur but was reclassified as a mesoeucrocodylian by Paul Barrett and Xing Xu in 2005.
A 2005 study by Barrett and Xu determined that the specimens originally assigned to Dianchungosaurus formed a chimera of different animals.
The name Dianchungosaurus lufengensis is retained for the holotype to maintain stability in the literature, while the paratype awaits formal description.
